name: Vultee BT-13 Valiant
summary: Fixed-gear WWII basic trainer, the 'Vibrator', used by most American pilots as the second stage between primary and advanced training; many survive in private hands.

wings: Low wing with a straight, tapered outer panel and slight dihedral at the tips
Wide centre section with simple flaps
engines: Large Pratt & Whitney Wasp Junior radial in a smooth round cowl
fuselage: Long glazed greenhouse over tandem seats
Fixed main gear (with fairings on early BT-13)
Deep, rounded fuselage with a metal skin
tail: Braced horizontal tail with a fabric-covered look

tellTales: Big radial nose and a long greenhouse over tandem seats on a fixed-gear low-wing
Fixed landing gear on a fairly large, heavy-looking trainer
Rounded rudder and a deep, round-bellied fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Texan has retractable gear, a bigger canopy hump and a more angular wing and tail; the Valiant has fixed gear and a rounded profile.
The Cornell is a smaller airplane with a slim nose or small radial; the Valiant has a big Wasp radial and a long greenhouse.
The Texan II is a modern turboprop with retractable gear; the Valiant has a big piston radial and fixed gear.
